text:
sneha: Heads-up — Prom billing spike this morning, looks like per-GPU + pod labels exploded cardinality on the cluster. Noticing huge scrape payloads from node-exporter/DCGM sidecars and a number of batch jobs hitting Pushgateway. Example metric snapshot we saw in logs:

```
gpu_memory_used_bytes{node="gpu-node-14", gpu_index="3", pod="training-job-42", container="trainer", model="gpt3-large", run_id="run-20250312-abc123"} 1.2e9
```

sneha: That run_id + model + pod combination is totally ephemeral and is creating millions of unique series over time. Any quick thoughts on mitigation? :eyes:

aj: I saw the same in grafana — per-node series count went from ~180k -> 1.7M. Alerts for Prometheus TSDB disk pressure triggered around 07:40 UTC. :fire:

maria: Pushgateway culprit: some batch jobs push per-task metrics with task_id label. We should not push high-cardinality IDs. Would like to throttle or sanitize pushes first.

kai: For node exporters / DCGM sidecars we can normalise labels in scrape config with relabel_configs to drop ephemeral labels. Two-phase plan: 1) relabel in scrape (dry-run), 2) update exporters to stop emitting the labels at source.

patrick: Agree. Also consider recording rules to aggregate at ingestion so we avoid storing raw high-cardinality series long-term.

sneha: Quick relabel snippet I tested locally — drops run_id/task_id/model when they look like GUIDs or are too high-cardinality:

```yaml
- job_name: 'gpu_exporters'
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['10.0.32.14:9100']
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: ['__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_run_id']
      regex: ".+"
      action: replace
      replacement: "__removed"
      target_label: '__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_run_id'
    - regex: '__removed'
      action: labeldrop
      replacement: ''
      source_labels: ['__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_run_id']
```

aj: That works but be careful — labeldrop vs replacement ordering matters. Also we should add a regex filter to allow known static model names (e.g., "resnet|bert|gpt2-small") and drop everything else.

maria: For Pushgateway, short-term we can add an admission hook: reject pushes containing label task_id or run_id, return 400. Long-term, change jobs to use job-level labels and a recording rule for task success rate.

kai: Ops checklist I'm proposing:
- Add relabel_configs in staging to drop ephemeral labels (dry-run flag enabled)
- Deploy a Pushgateway admission filter (sidecar) to reject high-cardinality pushes
- Add recording rules to compress time-series for 7d -> 1d resolutions
- Update node-exporter/DCGM to remove "model" label or map model -> family (coarse-grained)

sneha: Can someone paste the promtool/alert tweak we used to avoid noisy SLO alerts while we remediate? We muted the cardinality-driven alerts but kept disk-pressure ones.

patrick: We did a temporary alert inhibition rule in Alertmanager — inhibit series_count_alert if label cluster="canary" OR team="ml-platform" AND set a 4h window. Also lowered the evaluation frequency for the heavy rule from 1m -> 5m. Example alert tweak:

```yaml
- alert: HighSeriesCardinalityPerNode
  expr: increase(prometheus_tsdb_head_series{job="prometheus"}[5m]) > 10000
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Series count jump on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```

patrick: Change eval_interval on that rule to 5m in rule group meta while we stabilise.

aj: Also recommend enabling metric relabelling on Prometheus remote_write to reduce cardinality before it hits long-term storage (downsample or drop unwanted labels). Our remote accepts relabeling config so it can avoid egress costs.

maria: Ops cost note — we saw remote_write egress spike too because we were shipping all series to long-term. Dropping ephemeral series at scrape saves both TSDB storage and remote egress costs.

kai: I created a small canary daemonset that updates node-exporter args to map model label -> model_family with a small mapping config. Rolling it to 10% of nodes first. If no anomalies, increase rollout.

sneha: Timeline? We need a remediation plan within 4 hours to avoid touching SLOs for customers.

kai: Plan for next 4 hours:
1) 0-30m: Apply relabel_configs in staging Prom scrape (dry-run collect) and Pushgateway admission rule in staging.
2) 30-90m: Roll daemonset to 10% nodes (node-exporter relabeling/mapping).
3) 90-180m: Extend to 50% if metrics look stable, enable recording rules to compress historical noise.
4) 180-240m: Full rollout and remove short-term alert inhibitions if series counts stabilise.

maria: I'll own Pushgateway admission patch + docs for job owners. aj will help test Grafana dashboards to ensure SLO panels still render aggregated numbers.

aj: On it. I'll add a dashboard panel that shows series churn (new series per minute) and a heatmap of label cardinality by label name so we can watch model/run_id/task_id specifically.

infra-bot: deploy job started: daemonset/gpu-exporter-mapper canary -> 3/3 ready on nodepool/gpu-canary (id: deploy-2030456912)

kai: Thanks infra-bot — I'll monitor the canary. If anyone spots missing important telemetry, ping me. We'll keep historical retention for raw series for 24h then drop.

sneha: Thanks team. After this we should add a short section to the runbook: "what to do when cardinality spikes" with the relabel snippets and Pushgateway guidance.

patrick: Agreed — leaving a postmortem / follow-up doc after stabilisation. :thumbsup:
